name: cache-statusband
description: Nate Herk's Cache Keeper plus a ccstatusline-style status band: model, effort, context, cache, 5-hour/weekly/Fable usage with resets, and reopened chats measured before you send

author.name: Hameishiv, built on Cache Keeper by Nate Herk

seatFileTerminal.title: Seat file (terminal)
seatFileTerminal.description: For account rotators: a file holding the active seat's label (e.g. ~/.claude-cli-accounts/.active). Read when a session starts: the band shows that label in place of the account email. A running session keeps its account, so a change counts only once the rotator's wake-up prompt (below) reaches it, or within 3 minutes after it. Leave empty to show the account email.

seatFileDesktop.title: Seat file (desktop app)
seatFileDesktop.description: The same for sessions the desktop app runs, so each seat keeps its own usage reading. The app's band doesn't show it. Leave empty to turn off.

rotatorWakePattern.title: Rotator wake-up pattern
rotatorWakePattern.description: A regular expression matching the prompt an unattended account rotator types after rotating. Such a prompt is compacted first without asking, since nobody is there to answer, whenever the cold-send guard would apply: the guard is on (/cache guard off turns it off), the context is at least the big size (/cache big) and at least 100k tokens above what the last compaction left, the prompt has no attachment, the chat was not just compacted, and it is not typed inside a running turn. Otherwise it is sent as it is, uncompacted. For 3 minutes after it, a late rewrite of the seat file or the account is still taken as that rotation. Leave empty to turn off.

prPattern.title: PR session pattern
prPattern.description: A regular expression whose first group is a PR number, matched against any prompt while the session has no PR tracked, and against a resumed session's transcript (e.g. (?:^|\s)/?merge-pr\s+#?(\d+)). Keep warm then stops once gh reports that PR merged or closed. Leave empty to turn off.

autoResume.title: Auto-resume after usage renews
autoResume.description: When a chat's turn is cut short because the plan's usage ran out, send it "Resume" a minute after the full window resets. Spends usage without asking, so it is off by default. What arms it: Only usage exhaustion. A short throttle or an overload does not. What settles it: A message that reaches the chat settles it: the request that message starts (any main-loop request; a subagent's does not) removes the pending resume, so a later account change does not bring it back. /clear and resuming another chat cancel it too. A branch does not: it carries the conversation on, so a pending Resume, or one that is compacting, goes on in the branch. Rotator wake-ups: A rotator's wake-up is itself the resume. A due resume waits from the wake-up's arrival until its request starts. A wake-up that is cancelled (a message of yours reached the chat while it compacted, or the chat was cleared) arms no Resume in its place, so with auto-resume off no Resume is ever sent. What leaves it pending: A local command such as /usage, /cache or a typed /branch; a message another hook drops; a send you cancel in the cold-send dialog. /plan with a description is not local: it goes to the model unless the chat is already in plan mode, where it only shows the plan. A mod is not told the permission mode, so it counts as a send either way. The cold-send guard skips the same local commands, with these differences: /btw with a question sends the chat to the model, so on a cold chat it gets the dialog. A bare /btw stays local. So does /btw with a question while a turn is running, because that turn's requests keep the cache warm. /permissions and /login are skipped too, but they count as sends, because they open their own dialog first. What makes a due resume wait: It waits while the guard's dialog is open. It waits while any send handed on that is not this mod's own is being handed on, or has not yet started its request (for at most 2 minutes). It waits while a compaction before your send is running. When it is tried: A resume still pending that was armed from a full window is tried a minute after the account changes (a rotator's wake-up), not at that window's reset, because the window was the old account's. A failure from a request that was still out when the account changed is retried a minute later too, without counting as a try. With no known reset time it tries hourly, three times at most. Compacting first: On a big chat the Resume compacts first. While that runs, these cancel it: a message that reaches the chat (another plugin's too), a rotator wake-up arriving, /clear, and resuming another chat. These do not: a local command, a branch, and a message another hook drops. A wake-up that arrives while the Resume compacts waits for that compaction and uses it if it succeeded. A cold-send dialog open during the compaction: A dialog open for a message of yours holds the Resume until it closes. Cancel lets it go. Send anyway or Compact first cancels it (a /btw question does not: it never reaches the chat). If no request of any message starts within 2 minutes after such a cancel (for example a "Compact first" on a slash message, which goes back to the prompt box), the Resume is armed again 2 minutes after the cancel, and the band shows resumes meanwhile. If its compaction succeeded, it goes without compacting again (nor does a "Compact first" answered after it compact again). A failed compaction: If the Resume's compaction failed and you answered Cancel on a cold-send dialog for a message of yours while it compacted, the Resume is not sent uncompacted. It is armed again 2 minutes later and compacts again. If that compaction fails too, it is not sent at all, and a toast says to send Resume yourself. For a /btw question, an answer other than Cancel (such as Send anyway) does not count: the Resume goes as typed. For an ordinary message, Send anyway cancels the Resume, which is then armed again. A compaction that hangs: A compaction still running after 15 minutes is abandoned, so a hung one does not hold the Resume, a message or a wake-up for good. It may still finish, and until it does no send starts another compaction. The message you chose "Compact first" for, the wake-up's, and any send that was waiting on that compaction go back in the prompt box together, in the order sent, as one text. None of them is sent uncompacted, and neither is the Resume itself. A slash command is never joined with other text: a toast quotes it to send again. The Resume is tried again 2 minutes later without starting another compaction while the abandoned one is still out. That is a counted try, four in all, and the last toast names the cause of the last failed try: a send refused, or compaction not finished. If the abandoned compaction finishes later and succeeded, the chat counts as compacted and later sends go without compacting again. Putting a message back in the prompt box: The mod never rewrites text it did not put there. A message put back while text this mod left in the box is still unsent goes in behind that text when the message does not come from the prompt box (a remote or bridge send, such as a wake-up delivered remotely). A message you send from the prompt box takes the box's text with it, as any submit from the prompt box does, so it is put back on its own. The box is read when the engine allows it. If it is empty (text you deleted does not come back), or holds exactly the text this mod last put back (a trailing newline or CRLF line ends do not count), the new text is added behind it. If it holds anything else (a draft you are typing, or your edit of the put-back text), it is left exactly as it is. The put-back text is no longer remembered, and each message is quoted in full in a toast instead ("Also not sent: <text> — send it again when ready."). That toast holds a due Resume just as a put-back does. A read that the engine does not answer within 2 seconds, or that fails, shows nothing about the box. The box is left alone and each message is quoted the same way. The remembered put-back text is not used then, because it may be text you have since edited or deleted. A read that shows the box empty ends it. A slash command is never joined with other text and is quoted in full in a toast instead. When the box holds a slash command this mod put back and plain text is put back, the text is filled and the command quoted. A slash command or refused message put back after a compaction that finished goes the same way. The cold-send dialog then offers only Send anyway and Cancel, and says an earlier compaction is still running. How long the put-back text is remembered: With no time limit, until a message is handed on, a request starts, or you clear the chat or resume another. A branch keeps it, unless you typed it as a command: anything you submit from the prompt box, /branch included, takes the text in the box, so it ends the remembered text, and the Resume hold too when the message was put back in the box (not when it was only quoted in a toast). The remembered text is used in place of a read only when the engine has no way to read the box. A fill of the box that does not answer: A fill that does not answer within 2 seconds may still land. The toast says the message "may not have been put back" (after a compaction that was abandoned; after one that finished it says "Compacted, but the message may not have been sent again", and when that compaction failed, "The message may not have been sent again"), and quotes it in full. Nothing waits on it, the box counts as unknown (no put-back text is remembered), and the message holds a due Resume as a put-back does. While that fill is still out, a put-back quotes its message and leaves the box alone, even when a read shows the box empty. "Still out" lasts until it answers or fails, with 15 minutes as the limit for one that never does, and it holds across a /clear or a resume, because the prompt box is shared. The engine's own timeout for a fill is 5 seconds for each client it tries in turn, so a fill can answer well after 7 seconds. An answer that says it did not fill may be only the engine giving up, with the text still to be written. So the Resume stops waiting for that message only if the box, read afterwards, shows the text is not in it. With no way to read the box, or a read that fails or does not answer, it keeps waiting, for 15 minutes at most. That ends only the wait that fill started. A message quoted in a toast earlier keeps holding (15 minutes after it was quoted). When the fill was joined behind an earlier put-back still shown in the box, that put-back keeps holding and is remembered again. With no way to read the box, a late answer that did not fill makes the earlier put-back's text the remembered text again. This is best effort: the box most likely still starts with it, and if the engine writes the joined text after all, the next put-back may replace the newer part. A late answer that filled makes the text it filled (joined or not) the remembered one, so a later put-back goes in behind it. Neither is remembered if you submitted from the prompt box, a message was handed on or a request started meanwhile, or another put-back was started since. A fill that lands after you submitted something from the prompt box (which ended the wait and the remembered text) starts the wait again, and remembers the text when a read of the box shows it there. With no way to read the box, or a read that fails or does not answer, it starts the wait again but remembers nothing. Only a read that works and does not show the text starts nothing. Once it has answered, or the 15 minutes have passed, a put-back on an engine that can read the box reads it and leaves it alone unless it is empty. On an engine with no way to read it, with no put-back text remembered, the box is overwritten. What a pending Resume waits for after a put-back: It waits until you send what was put back, you clear the chat, you submit a command or other text from the prompt box over a message that was put back in it, or 15 minutes have passed since the put-back. So it never goes ahead of a message you still have to send. A message only quoted in the toast was never in the box, so it keeps holding, also when another message was put back in the box after it. While it waits, the band shows Resume waits for your message instead of a time. A message that could not be put back, or a /btw question (it never reaches the chat), holds nothing and ends nothing: the wait for an earlier message stays as it was. A compaction from a chat that was cleared or replaced: It is never remembered and never counts for the new chat. A message waiting on it is not sent into the new chat, nor put back in its box. A toast says "Not sent, because the chat was cleared", or "... was replaced by a resumed chat", and quotes the message in full. A branch carries the conversation on, so its message is sent, and a compaction in flight when you branch stays that conversation's: it is waited for, and its end or abandonment counts as before. A message whose chat is cleared while it is being put back gets the toast "The chat was cleared while your message was being put back: <text>" (or "... replaced by a resumed chat ..."), because the text may already be in the box. What the fill left out is quoted in full as usual. The message is dropped when that compaction ends, and is not held on a compaction of the new chat. A send in the new chat does not wait on it. While it is still out, the engine's compaction notices are ignored, so its late end does not mark the new chat compacted (a compaction out for more than 30 minutes no longer counts). When the compaction mark is forgotten: When any later compaction succeeds (your own /compact too), once a second 15 minutes have passed, and on /clear or resuming another chat. A compaction that started before a newer abandoned one does not forget that one. Nor does an engine compaction notice while an older compaction of this mod is still out and started under 30 minutes ago, because it may be that one's end. When the Resume cannot be sent: Whether directly or after compacting, it is tried again 2 minutes later, four attempts in all, then a toast says to send it yourself. A request that starts, or a chat that is cleared or replaced meanwhile, settles it, so it is not tried again into that chat. Desktop app: The app's "Try again" prompt is drawn by the app itself, which a mod cannot remove, so it may stay on screen. The resume goes to the session either way.
